title: How to use the Content Hub in Keynote on Mac: steps for Keynote 15.4
metaTitle: How to use the Content Hub in Keynote on Mac
description: How to use the Content Hub in Keynote on Mac: add Apple-curated images, replace them, and remove watermarks with a subscription.
targetKeyword: how to use the content hub in keynote on mac
intro: To use the Content Hub in Keynote on Mac, click its toolbar button, pick a category at the top of the dialog, then click a premium image. Anyone can use the premium images, but without an Apple Creator Studio subscription they carry a watermark.
tldr: Click the Content Hub button in Keynote's toolbar, pick a category at the top of the dialog, then click a premium image.
Premium Content Hub images work without a subscription, but they carry a watermark until you subscribe.
Apple Creator Studio costs $12.99 a month or $129 a year for new subscribers, after a one-month free trial.
Apple documents no keyboard shortcut for opening the Content Hub. Shift-click selects several images at once.
To replace an image, use the Replace button in the Format sidebar's Image tab. Keynote 15.4 needs macOS 26 or later.

blocks.text: What the Content Hub is and where it lives

The Content Hub is a library of Apple-curated photos, illustrations, graphics and backgrounds. You open it from inside Keynote, so you never download a file and drag it in. Apple's marketing page says the same library is also reached from Pages, Numbers and Freeform.

Content Hub is a subscriber feature. Keynote 15.1 brought it into Apple Creator Studio in early 2026, alongside Pages and Numbers. Creating, viewing, editing and real-time collaboration don't require a subscription, according to Apple's What's New page.
So the short version is this. You can insert premium Content Hub images without paying. The catch is the watermark, and a subscription removes it.
What it costs and what a subscription adds

Apple Creator Studio costs $12.99 a month or $129 a year for new subscribers, after a one-month free trial. Students and educators pay $2.99 a month or $29.99 a year after verification. These are US dollars, taken from Apple's own pricing page.
Buying a new iPad or Mac gets you three months free. After that, the price is the same. Standard plans can be shared with up to five other family members through Family Sharing.

The subscription also comes with limits. Macworld reports that subscribers can generate up to 50 AI images and 50 presentations of about 10 slides each per month. Those limits cover AI features. Apple's notes don't say that the Content Hub library has a monthly cap.
Check your Keynote and macOS versions first
Content Hub needs a recent Keynote. Keynote 15.1 added it as a subscriber feature. Keynote 15.3 made replacing images from the Content Hub easier for everyone. Keynote 15.4 is the current version.

Apple's pages don't agree on the macOS number, though. Apple's What's New page says Keynote 15.4 needs macOS 26 or later. Its Creator Studio support page says full Creator Studio functionality comes with macOS 27. TidBITS listed different numbers for Keynote 15.1 altogether. Start with the What's New page, then check the others if something is missing.

blocks.title: Check your version
blocks.text: Open the Keynote menu and choose About Keynote. Compare the version number with 15.4. If you're on an older version, update Keynote in the App Store before you follow the steps in this guide.
Add a premium image to a slide
Open the deck and select the slide that needs the picture. Keynote places the new image on the slide you are viewing, so check the thumbnail first. A wrong slide is an easy mistake to make.

The Content Hub button is an icon in the toolbar. Apple's help doesn't name it in words, so you may need to check a few icons before you find it. It sits near the object buttons, the ones that add things such as tables and charts.
When the dialog opens, look for the object categories across the top. Apple's help says to click one. It doesn't list the categories by name, so browse until one fits the slide.
Pick the right category and image

rows: Opens Content Hub. Shown as an icon, not a word.
Check each toolbar icon until you find it.
Object categories you click to narrow the view.
Start broad, then click one that fits your slide.
Click it to add it to the slide.
Check for a watermark if you aren't subscribed.
blocks.caption: The parts of the dialog that Apple's help covers

blocks.text: Search, filters and layout are not documented. If nothing fits, switch categories instead of scrolling one long list. That's quicker, and it helps you see what the library holds.
Pick an image that leaves room for your text. A photo with a clear side works best for a title slide. Test two or three options on the slide before you commit to one.
Replace an image you already placed
You don't need to delete a picture to swap it. Keynote can replace it in place, which saves you from resizing the new one. Apple says the new image keeps the original dimensions.

There are two routes. The first is the Replace Image button in the bottom-right corner of a media placeholder. Click it, choose the image, then double-click it. The second works on any selected image. Open the Image tab in the Format sidebar and click Replace.
Replacement can fail when an image is locked or grouped. Remove the lock or ungroup it first, then try again. Apple's help gives that as the cause, so check it before you try anything else.
Select and work with several images
Hold Shift and click each image you want. Keynote selects them together, so you can work with several at once. This is handy when a slide needs a row of pictures.
Apple's help doesn't list every action that works on a multi-selection. If you aren't sure, test one image first, then apply the same change to the group.
Remove watermarks with an Apple Creator Studio subscription

A watermark is the visible sign of a Content Hub image used without a subscription. Apple says anyone can use premium images, but you need a subscription to remove the watermark. TidBITS adds a licensing limit. Content Hub items can't be used as standalone files outside Creator Studio apps.

To subscribe, open the Keynote menu and choose Get Apple Creator Studio. Then complete the prompts. To cancel or change a plan later, open the Keynote menu and choose Manage Subscription. That option opens the App Store.
If your subscription doesn't show when you manage it, sign in to your Apple Account in the App Store. Apple's help says to check that first.

What happens when the subscription ends? Apple says you keep access to Keynote, Pages, Numbers and Freeform without the intelligence features. You also keep your projects and files. Apple's pages don't say whether watermarks come back on images you already placed, so check those slides before you present.
Common problems and what to check

items: Button missing: right-click the toolbar, choose Customize Toolbar, and drag the Content Hub icon back on. Then click Done.
Watermarks on images: subscribe through Keynote > Get Apple Creator Studio, then confirm you're signed in to the App Store.
Replace won't work: remove any lock or ungroup the image first, then try again.
Feature missing: check macOS. Keynote 15.4 needs macOS 26 or later, and Apple ties full Creator Studio functionality to macOS 27.
Keynote for iCloud: Apple's pages don't confirm Content Hub support on the web. Use the Mac app for this step.

blocks.text: Mistakes people make with the Content Hub

items: Looking for a keyboard shortcut. Apple documents none for the Content Hub, so use the toolbar button.
Assuming a watermark-free image without a subscription. Free use still gets the watermark.
Deleting an image and adding a new one, then resizing it again. Replace the image instead, so the dimensions carry over.
Trying to export a Content Hub image as its own file. The license keeps it inside Creator Studio apps.
Checking only the Keynote version. macOS matters too, and Apple's pages disagree on the number.

blocks.text: Keyboard shortcuts and what Apple documents
Apple's help documents no keyboard shortcut for opening the Content Hub. Don't search a shortcut list for one. The toolbar button is the documented way in.
Shift-click is the only shortcut-style step in this guide. Hold Shift and click images to select several at once. Apple's help covers that step directly.
Stock video and what is coming next

Apple's October 27, 2026 newsroom release says Content Hub expands to Apple-curated stock video across Keynote, Pages and Numbers. It says the update arrives on the App Store in November, as a free update for existing subscribers.
This guide doesn't confirm that the video update has shipped. If you need video in a deck, check the App Store update list first. The photo steps in this guide work the same way either way.
Where to go next with your slides

Once an image is on the slide, you may want to change its shape. [How to mask an image in Keynote on Mac](/how-to/mask-an-image-in-keynote) covers three ways to do that. If you use a picture as the slide background, [How to add a background image in Keynote on Mac](/how-to/add-a-background-image-in-keynote) shows the steps.

When the deck is final, [export it as a PDF](/how-to/export-a-presentation-as-a-pdf-in-keynote) so the layout stays fixed on another computer. If you aren't subscribed, look at the watermark in the PDF before you send it.

If your slide also needs motion, [How to animate an object in Keynote on Mac](/how-to/animate-an-object-in-keynote) covers the steps. Play the slide once before you present, and check that the picture still looks right.

faq.question: Is the Content Hub free in Keynote on Mac?
faq.answer: The Content Hub belongs to Apple Creator Studio. You can insert premium images without a subscription, but they carry a watermark. A subscription removes the watermark. Apple lists $12.99 a month or $129 a year after a one-month trial.

faq.question: Do I need a subscription to open the Content Hub?
faq.answer: Apple's help says anyone can use premium Content Hub images. The subscription matters for the watermark. Creating, viewing and editing your deck don't require a subscription.

faq.question: Which Keynote version has the Content Hub?
faq.answer: Keynote 15.1 added it as a subscriber feature in early 2026. Keynote 15.3 made replacing images from it easier for everyone. Keynote 15.4 is the current version and needs macOS 26 or later.

faq.question: What macOS do I need for the Content Hub?
faq.answer: Apple's What's New page says Keynote 15.4 needs macOS 26 or later. Its Creator Studio support page says full Creator Studio functionality needs macOS 27. Check both pages if a feature is missing from your Mac.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for the Content Hub?
faq.answer: Apple documents none. Click the Content Hub button in the toolbar to open it. Use Shift-click to select several images at once.

faq.question: Can I use a Content Hub image outside Keynote?
faq.answer: Not as a standalone file. TidBITS reports that the license limits Content Hub items to Creator Studio apps. Keep the image inside your slides and export the deck instead.

faq.question: What happens to my images if I cancel my subscription?
faq.answer: Apple says you keep access to Keynote without the intelligence features, and you keep your projects and files. Apple's pages don't say whether watermarks return on images you already placed, so check your slides.

faq.question: Does Keynote for iCloud have the Content Hub?
faq.answer: Apple's pages I read don't confirm Content Hub support in Keynote for iCloud. Test it in the browser before you depend on it, or use the Keynote app on your Mac.

faq.question: Can I replace an image without losing its size?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the Replace Image button on a media placeholder, or click Replace in the Image tab of the Format sidebar. Apple says the new image keeps the original dimensions.

steps.name: Open the slide you want to change
steps.text: Open your deck in Keynote and select the slide that needs the picture. A new image lands on the slide you are viewing. Check the thumbnail before you go on.
steps.tip: Select the slide in the navigator, then look at the canvas to confirm it is the right one.

steps.name: Find the Content Hub button
steps.text: Look along the toolbar for the Content Hub button. Apple's help shows it as an icon, not a word, so you may need to check a few icons. It sits near the object buttons.

steps.name: Open the Content Hub
steps.text: Click the Content Hub button. The dialog opens with object categories across the top. Apple's help doesn't name the categories, so read the labels as you go.

steps.name: Pick an object category
steps.text: Click the category that fits your slide. If nothing fits, try another category instead of scrolling one long list.

steps.name: Click a premium image
steps.text: Scroll the results and find an image you want. Apple calls these premium images. Click the image to add it to the slide.

steps.name: Check the watermark
steps.text: If you aren't subscribed, the image carries a watermark. To remove it, subscribe to Apple Creator Studio from the Keynote menu, then look at the slide again.
steps.tip: Apple says a subscription removes the watermark, so check the slide after you subscribe.

steps.name: Resize or move the image
steps.text: Drag a corner handle to resize the image, and drag the middle to move it. Size the frame before you replace an image, since the new one keeps the original dimensions.
steps.tip: Locked or grouped images may not resize. Remove the lock or ungroup them first.

steps.name: Replace an image you already placed
steps.text: Select the image, open the Image tab in the Format sidebar, and click Replace. Choose the new image. The new image keeps the original dimensions.

steps.name: Select several images
steps.text: Hold Shift and click each image you want. Keynote selects them together, so you can work with several at once.

shortcuts.action: Open Content Hub: no documented shortcut, use the toolbar

troubleshooting.problem: The Content Hub button is missing from the toolbar
troubleshooting.fix: Right-click the toolbar and choose Customize Toolbar. If the icon was dragged off, drag it back onto the toolbar, then click Done. A third-party guide, Kirkville, describes these steps for iWork apps.

You may not be subscribed. Choose Keynote > Get Apple Creator Studio to subscribe. If the watermark stays, sign in to your Apple Account in the App Store and check again. Apple's notes don't document a fix for that case.
The image may be locked or grouped. Select it, turn off the lock in the Arrange menu or use Arrange > Ungroup, then try the replace again.

troubleshooting.problem: A Content Hub feature described by Apple is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Check your macOS version. Keynote 15.4 needs macOS 26 or later. Apple's Creator Studio page ties full functionality to macOS 27, so update macOS before you assume a fault in Keynote.

troubleshooting.problem: You are looking for Content Hub stock video
troubleshooting.fix: Apple said on October 27, 2026 that stock video would arrive in November, as a free update for subscribers. Check the App Store update list in November. This guide doesn't confirm that it has shipped.

troubleshooting.problem: Keynote for iCloud doesn't show the Content Hub
troubleshooting.fix: Apple's pages don't confirm Content Hub support in Keynote for iCloud. Use the Keynote app on your Mac for this step.
